title: 3.1 Cell Theory
description: The three principles of cell theory and its historical development

questions.question: What are the three principles of the cell theory?
options: All living things are composed of cells, cells are the basic unit of life, all cells come from pre-existing cells
Cells contain DNA, cells perform photosynthesis, cells are microscopic
All cells are identical, cells need energy, cells have cell walls
Cells have nuclei, cells require oxygen, cells reproduce by mitosis
questions.explanation: The three principles state: (1) all living things are composed of cells, (2) cells are the basic unit of structure and function in living things, and (3) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Who was the first person to observe cells using a microscope?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke (1665) observed thin slices of cork under a microscope and described small box-like structures which he called 'cells'.

questions.question: Which scientist concluded that all plants are made of cells?
questions.explanation: Matthias Schleiden (1838) concluded that all plant tissues are composed of cells.

questions.question: Which scientist concluded that all animals are made of cells?
questions.explanation: Theodor Schwann (1839) concluded that all animal tissues are composed of cells, extending cell theory to animals.

questions.question: Who added the principle that all cells arise from pre-existing cells?
questions.explanation: Rudolf Virchow (1855) proposed 'Omnis cellula e cellula' — all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exception to the cell theory?
questions.explanation: Viruses are considered exceptions to cell theory because they are acellular — they are not made of cells and cannot reproduce independently.

questions.question: What material did Robert Hooke examine when he first discovered cells?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke examined thin slices of cork (dead plant cell walls) under a compound microscope in 1665.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Latin phrase 'Omnis cellula e cellula'?
options: Cells are the basic unit of life
Cells are found in all living things
All cells arise from pre-existing cells
questions.explanation: This phrase, proposed by Rudolf Virchow, means 'every cell from a cell' — all cells come from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Why is striated muscle tissue considered an exception to cell theory?
options: It does not come from pre-existing cells
It contains very large, multinucleated cells that challenge the definition of a single cell
It is not made of cells
questions.explanation: Striated muscle fibers are very long and contain many nuclei, making it difficult to define where one cell ends and another begins.

questions.question: Which statement about cells is NOT part of the cell theory?
options: All cells arise from pre-existing cells
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life
All living organisms are composed of one or more cells
questions.explanation: The statement 'all cells contain a nucleus' is not part of cell theory — prokaryotic cells (bacteria) lack a nucleus.

questions.question: In what year did Robert Hooke first observe and name cells?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke published his observations of cork cells in his book 'Micrographia' in 1665.

questions.question: The giant alga Acetabularia is an exception to cell theory because it is:
options: A single cell that can grow up to several centimeters in length
Made of many small cells joined together
questions.explanation: Acetabularia is a giant single-celled alga that can grow to 2-6 cm, challenging the typical view of cells as microscopic.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the contribution of Antonie van Leeuwenhoek to cell biology?
options: He proposed that all plants are made of cells
He added the principle of biogenesis to cell theory
He was the first to observe living cells using a microscope
questions.explanation: Van Leeuwenhoek improved microscopes and was the first to observe living microorganisms (which he called 'animalcules'), bacteria, and protozoa.

questions.question: What does the first principle of cell theory state?
options: Cells can arise spontaneously from non-living matter
Cells are the basic unit of reproduction
All living things are composed of one or more cells
questions.explanation: The first principle states that all living organisms are composed of one or more cells.

questions.question: What does the second principle of cell theory state?
options: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life
All cells come from pre-existing cells
Cells can be seen without a microscope
questions.explanation: The second principle states that the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function in living organisms.

questions.question: What does the third principle of cell theory state?
options: All cells are surrounded by a cell wall
All living things are made of cells
The cell is the basic unit of life
All cells arise from pre-existing cells
questions.explanation: The third principle states that all cells arise only from pre-existing cells (biogenesis), refuting spontaneous generation.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is NOT composed of cells?
questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular — they consist of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat but are not made of cells.

questions.question: How did the invention of the microscope contribute to the development of cell theory?
options: It demonstrated that cells do not reproduce
It allowed scientists to see cells and their structures for the first time
It showed that all cells are identical
It proved spontaneous generation of cells
questions.explanation: The microscope enabled scientists to observe cells directly, leading to the discoveries that formed the basis of cell theory.

questions.question: What is the main difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms according to cell theory?
options: Unicellular organisms consist of a single cell, while multicellular organisms consist of many cells
Multicellular organisms do not come from pre-existing cells
questions.explanation: Unicellular organisms (e.g., bacteria, amoeba) are made of one cell, while multicellular organisms (e.g., humans, trees) are composed of many cells.

questions.question: Why is spontaneous generation rejected by cell theory?
options: Cells have been observed arising spontaneously in laboratories
All known evidence shows that cells only arise from pre-existing cells
Spontaneous generation only applies to plants
questions.explanation: Cell theory's third principle (biogenesis) states that cells come only from pre-existing cells, rejecting the idea of spontaneous generation.

questions.question: Which two scientists are credited with formally proposing the cell theory in 1838-1839?
questions.explanation: Matthias Schleiden (plants, 1838) and Theodor Schwann (animals, 1839) together proposed that all living things are composed of cells.

questions.question: What is the term for the idea that life arises from non-living matter?
questions.explanation: Spontaneous generation (abiogenesis) is the disproven idea that living organisms can arise from non-living matter.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between cell theory and modern biology?
options: Cell theory remains a fundamental unifying concept in biology
Cell theory is outdated and no longer used
Cell theory only applies to plants
Cell theory has been replaced by molecular biology
questions.explanation: Cell theory is one of the fundamental unifying concepts in biology, providing the foundation for understanding life processes.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the 'cell' as named by Robert Hooke?
options: He was observing the empty cell walls of dead cork cells
He was observing living cells with nuclei
questions.explanation: Hooke observed dead cork cells and saw only the cell walls remaining, which he named 'cells' because they resembled small rooms.

questions.question: Why are mitochondria and chloroplasts sometimes considered exceptions to cell theory?
options: They are not made of cells
They contain their own DNA and reproduce independently within the cell, similar to bacteria
They are not found in eukaryotic cells
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA and ribosomes and reproduce by binary fission, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
